in_hebrew.name: ג'וליאנו
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא חנני, אלוהים הוא רחמי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ג'וליאנו מקורו בשם העברי יונתן, שפירושו אלוהים הוא חנני, אלוהים הוא רחמי. השם יונתן מוזכר בתנ"ך, בספר שמואל, כבן של שאול המלך וכאחד מהדמויות המרכזיות בתקופת המלכים. השם ג'וליאנו הוא גרסה איטלקית של השם יוליאנוס, שגם הוא קשור לשם יונתן.

in_greek.name: Γιουλιάνω
in_greek.meaning: ο Θεός είναι ευγενικός, ο Θεός είναι συμπονετικός
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Giuliano προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Julianus, το οποίο συνδέεται με το ελληνικό όνομα Ιουλιανός. Το όνομα Julianus πιθανότατα προέρχεται από το όνομα Ιούλιος, που σημαίνει "απόγονος του Ιούλιος" ή "ευγενής". Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει συγκεκριμένη αναφορά στο όνομα Giuliano, αλλά το όνομα Julianus αναφέρεται σε αρκετές προσωπικότητες της Ρωμαϊκής Αυτοκρατορίας.

in_latin.name: Giuliano
in_latin.meaning: Deus est misericors, Deus est gratiosus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Giuliano derivatum est a nomine Latino Julianus, quod significat "Deus est misericors" vel "Deus est gratiosus". Nomen Julianus a Romanorum familiae nobili Iulia ortum est. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Julianus gestum est a variis sanctis et episcopis, inter quos Julianus episcopus Calesii.

The name Giuliano is associated with several saints and has been popularized in Italy and other European countries.

data.cultural_impact: Giuliano is an Italian name derived from the Roman family name "Julius". In ancient Rome, the name Julius was given to a child born during the month of July, which was considered a time of renewal and growth. The name Giuliano carries this cultural significance of youthfulness and renewal in both the secular and religious contexts in Western society. In Italy, it was popularized by the Medici family, who ruled Florence during the Renaissance period and had several members named Giuliano.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Giuliano is associated with St. Jules (or Julius), a saint and martyr in the late 3rd or early 4th century. According to Christian tradition, St. Jules was a youth from Cilicia who converted to Christianity and was eventually put to death for his faith. He is venerated as a patron saint of Hatters, Knitters, Hatmakers, Breasts, childbirth, and May-making, and is believed to have the power to protect against epilepsy and to heal various types of skin diseases. Thus, the name Giuliano carries a profound spiritual significance for Christians, representing youthful devotion, faith, and the promise of eternal life.

historical_references.reference: Giuliano della Rovere (1443-1513) was an Italian statesman, condottiero, and poet, who became Pope under the name Julius II.
